markets.title: US Treasury yields surge to highest since 2007
markets.raw_summary: Benchmark 10-year hits 5.02% as investors continue to sell government debt in expectations of a Fed rate increase this week

insight.what: 基准 10 年期美债收益率升至 5.02%，为 2007 年以来最高，投资者抛售国债，预期美联储本周加息。
insight.why: 市场原本在定价加息周期接近尾声，现在重新提高本周加息和利率更久的预期；全球无风险利率上升，股债估值和美元都要重估。
insight.chain: 通胀和油价高位 → 市场预期 Fed 本周加息 → 投资者卖出美债 → 10Y 美债收益率升至 5.02% → 全球无风险利率 Rf 上升 → 高估值成长股折现率上升 → 股价承压；美元资产吸引力上升 → 美元走强 → 新兴市场资本外流压力
notes: 10 年期美债收益率是投资者持有美国十年期国债到期的年化回报，也是全球资产定价的无风险利率基准。
收益率上升，债券价格下跌：债券价格和收益率反向变动，因为新债利息更高时，旧债必须降价才有人买。
为什么加息预期会推高长端收益率？短期政策利率上升会带动整条利率曲线；同时市场担心通胀和国债供给，要求更高的期限溢价 term premium。
期限溢价是投资者持有长期债券而非滚动买短债所要求的额外补偿，财政赤字和通胀不确定性上升时它会变大。
为什么成长股受伤？成长股盈利多在未来，折现率上升时，未来现金流换算成今天的价值缩水更明显。
美元走强原因：美国利率上升，美元资产回报更高，全球资金买入美元，推高美元汇率。
新兴市场压力：美元走强和全球利率上升会提高新兴市场借美元的成本，并促使资金回流美国。

insight_en.what: The benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury yield rose to 5.02%, its highest level since 2007, as investors sold Treasuries in anticipation of a Federal Reserve rate hike this week.
insight_en.why: Markets had been pricing in the rate-hiking cycle nearing its end, but are now raising expectations again for a rate hike this week and for interest rates to stay higher for longer; global risk-free rates are rising, requiring equity and bond valuations and the U.S. dollar to be reassessed.
insight_en.chain: Inflation and oil prices remain high → Markets expect the Fed to raise rates this week → Investors sell U.S. Treasuries → 10Y U.S. Treasury yield rises to 5.02% → Global risk-free rate Rf rises → Discount rates for highly valued growth stocks rise → Stock prices come under pressure；U.S. dollar assets become more attractive → U.S. dollar strengthens → Emerging markets face capital outflow pressure
notes: The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield is the annualized return investors earn by holding a 10-year U.S. Treasury bond to maturity, and is also the benchmark risk-free rate for global asset pricing.
When yields rise, bond prices fall: bond prices and yields move in opposite directions because when new bonds pay higher interest, older bonds must fall in price to attract buyers.

Why do rate-hike expectations push up long-term yields? Rising short-term policy rates push up the entire yield curve; at the same time, concerns about inflation and Treasury supply lead the market to demand a higher term premium.

The term premium is the extra compensation investors demand for holding long-term bonds rather than rolling over investments in short-term bonds; it increases when fiscal deficits and inflation uncertainty rise.
Why are growth stocks hurt? Most growth-stock earnings lie in the future, so when the discount rate rises, the present value of future cash flows falls more sharply.
Why the U.S. dollar strengthens: U.S. interest rates rise, dollar assets offer higher returns, and global investors buy dollars, pushing up the dollar's exchange rate.
Pressure on emerging markets: a stronger dollar and higher global interest rates increase the cost of dollar borrowing for emerging markets and encourage capital to flow back to the United States.

markets.title: 日本财务大臣片山皋月：不会依靠赤字融资公债为减税措施筹措财源。 将同时检视支出与财政收入，以维护市场信心。 将从严审查下一财年各项预算申请。

insight.what: 日本财务大臣片山皋月表示，不会靠增发赤字公债为减税筹资，将检视收支并严审下一财年预算申请。
insight.why: 市场担心日本减税和国防开支会让国债发行增加、财政恶化；此番承诺压低日本国债期限溢价，支撑日元，并缓和全球债券收益率压力。
insight.chain: 财务大臣承诺不靠赤字公债 → 市场下调 JGB 供给预期 → JGB 期限溢价 term premium 下降 → JGB 收益率回落 → 日本财政风险溢价下降 → 日元资产吸引力上升 → 日元走强；财政刺激规模受限 → 日本内需预期降温 → 日股周期板块承压
notes: JGB 是日本国债，日本政府借钱的主要工具，其收益率是全球长期利率的重要参考之一。
期限溢价 term premium 是投资者持有长期债券要求的额外补偿，国债供给越多、财政越不确定，这个补偿越高。
日本财务大臣表态为什么重要？如果减税靠增发国债融资，JGB 供给会上升，收益率会被推高，并可能吸走海外债券配置资金。
财政风险溢价是投资者因为担心一国财政恶化而要求的额外回报，风险溢价下降会提升该国货币资产的吸引力。
日元走强不只由利差决定，也受财政纪律和市场信心影响；财政风险下降时，日元资产可能获得支撑。
如果财政刺激规模受限，日本内需相关行业盈利预期会降温，日股周期板块可能承压。

insight_en.what: Japan's Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said she would not fund tax cuts by issuing additional deficit-financing bonds, and would review revenue and expenditure and closely scrutinize budget requests for the next fiscal year.
insight_en.why: Markets were concerned that Japan's tax cuts and defense spending would increase government bond issuance and worsen its fiscal position; this commitment lowers the term premium on Japanese government bonds, supports the yen and eases pressure on global bond yields.
insight_en.chain: Finance minister pledges not to rely on deficit-financing bonds → Markets revise JGB supply expectations downward → JGB term premium declines → JGB yields fall → Japan's fiscal risk premium declines → Yen-denominated assets become more attractive → Yen strengthens；Scale of fiscal stimulus is constrained → Expectations for Japanese domestic demand cool → Cyclical sectors of Japan's stock market come under pressure
notes: JGBs are Japanese government bonds, the Japanese government's main borrowing instrument, and their yields are an important reference for global long-term interest rates.

The term premium is the additional compensation investors require for holding long-term bonds; the greater the supply of government bonds and the greater the fiscal uncertainty, the higher this compensation.

Why do the Japanese finance minister's remarks matter? If tax cuts are financed through additional government bond issuance, JGB supply will increase, pushing up yields and potentially drawing away funds allocated to overseas bonds.

The fiscal risk premium is the extra return investors demand because of concerns about deterioration in a country's fiscal position; a lower risk premium makes assets denominated in that country's currency more attractive.
Yen strength is determined not only by interest rate differentials, but also by fiscal discipline and market confidence; yen-denominated assets may receive support when fiscal risk declines.
If the scale of fiscal stimulus is constrained, earnings expectations for industries tied to Japanese domestic demand will cool, and cyclical sectors of Japan's stock market may come under pressure.

policy.title: China targets offshore operations of brokerages in crackdown on pay loopholes, corruption
policy.raw_summary: China’s securities regulator and its industry body are moving to close compensation loopholes for brokerage management and staff, extending anti-corruption oversight to overseas operations for the fir

insight.what: 中国证监会和行业协会收紧券商薪酬漏洞，并将监管延伸至券商离岸业务。
insight.why: 市场原本以为薪酬和反腐监管主要针对境内；离岸业务也被覆盖，中资券商跨境扩张的合规成本和收入不确定性上升，券商股和香港离岸资金流承压。
insight.chain: 监管堵住薪酬漏洞 → 券商合规成本上升 → 离岸业务扩张受限 → 跨境资本流动更受监控 → 中资券商境外收入预期下降 → 券商股盈利预测下调 → 港股中资券商承压；跨境资本流动监控趋严 → 离岸人民币 CNH 流动性收紧 → 人民币汇率波动加大
notes: 券商离岸业务是境内券商通过香港等境外子公司开展的国际业务，包括跨境投行、交易和资产管理。
薪酬漏洞指通过离岸子公司、奖金递延或费用报销等方式规避境内薪酬限制和监管。
为什么监管影响估值？合规成本上升和业务扩张放缓会压低未来利润，市场因此下调券商股盈利预期。
跨境资本流动监控变严，会影响离岸人民币 CNH 市场的资金进出和流动性。
香港是中资券商连接内地资本和全球市场的重要节点，所以香港券商股和港元流动性对这类监管更敏感。
这类政策信号还会影响外资对中国金融开放和监管可预测性的判断，进而影响中概金融股风险溢价。

insight_en.what: The China Securities Regulatory Commission and industry associations are closing loopholes in brokerage compensation and extending oversight to brokerages' offshore businesses.
insight_en.why: Markets had assumed that compensation and anti-corruption oversight primarily targeted domestic operations; with offshore businesses now also covered, compliance costs and revenue uncertainty for Chinese brokerages' cross-border expansion are rising, putting pressure on brokerage stocks and offshore capital flows in Hong Kong.
insight_en.chain: Regulators close compensation loopholes → Brokerages' compliance costs rise → Offshore business expansion is constrained → Cross-border capital flows face greater monitoring → Overseas revenue expectations for Chinese brokerages decline → Earnings forecasts for brokerage stocks are revised downward → Hong Kong-listed Chinese brokerages come under pressure；Monitoring of cross-border capital flows tightens → Offshore renminbi CNH liquidity tightens → Renminbi exchange rate volatility increases
notes: Brokerages' offshore businesses are the international operations conducted by domestic brokerages through overseas subsidiaries in places such as Hong Kong, including cross-border investment banking, trading and asset management.
Compensation loopholes refer to ways of circumventing domestic compensation limits and regulation through methods such as offshore subsidiaries, bonus deferrals or expense reimbursements.
Why does regulation affect valuations? Higher compliance costs and slower business expansion depress future profits, leading markets to lower earnings expectations for brokerage stocks.
Stricter monitoring of cross-border capital flows will affect fund inflows and outflows and liquidity in the offshore renminbi CNH market.

Hong Kong is an important hub through which Chinese brokerages connect mainland capital with global markets, so Hong Kong brokerage stocks and Hong Kong dollar liquidity are more sensitive to this type of regulation.

Such policy signals also affect foreign investors' assessments of the opening of China's financial sector and regulatory predictability, which in turn affect the risk premium on overseas-listed Chinese financial stocks.

tech.title: Trump, China Push Back on Calls to Slow AI
tech.raw_summary: Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang took a live phone call from Donald Trump during a panel discussion, where Trump dismissed artificial intelligence dangers as a “hoax.” Meanwhile, a Chinese

insight.what: 特朗普在英伟达 CEO 黄仁勋台上通话中拒绝放慢 AI 的呼吁，中国也反对放缓 AI。
insight.why: 市场原本担心 AI 安全监管和中美限制会拖慢算力投资；两国同时释放不减速信号，降低监管风险，强化芯片和算力资本开支预期，但加剧供应链割裂。
insight.chain: 中美均反对放缓 AI → AI 监管收紧预期下降 → 科技巨头资本开支更激进 → 算力芯片需求上升 → 先进制程和封装产能紧张 → 芯片供应链竞争加剧 → 芯片股盈利预期上修；地缘竞争 → 出口管制风险上升 → 供应链区域化 → 成本曲线抬升
notes: AI guardrails 是 AI 安全护栏，指对模型能力、数据使用和部署设置监管限制。
为什么芯片股对监管敏感？如果监管迫使 AI 公司放缓训练和部署，GPU 和先进芯片订单会下降。
资本开支是云厂商和科技公司购买服务器、芯片、建数据中心的支出，直接决定芯片需求。
先进制程和封装是制造高性能 AI 芯片的关键环节，产能紧张时芯片价格和利润率更坚挺。
出口管制会限制高端芯片和设备流向中国，迫使供应链分成不同区域，重复建设会抬高成本。
中美都不愿放慢 AI，意味着竞争优先于安全协调，长期来看政策反弹和供应链摩擦风险仍在。

insight_en.what: Trump rejected calls to slow AI during a call with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who was on stage, and China also opposed an AI slowdown.
insight_en.why: Markets had worried that AI safety regulation and U.S.-China restrictions would slow investment in computing capacity; simultaneous signals from both countries against a slowdown reduce regulatory risk and reinforce expectations for capital expenditure on chips and computing capacity, but deepen supply chain fragmentation.
insight_en.chain: Both China and the U.S. oppose slowing AI → Expectations of tighter AI regulation decline → Tech giants pursue more aggressive capital expenditure → Demand for compute chips rises → Advanced-node manufacturing and packaging capacity tightens → Competition in the chip supply chain intensifies → Earnings expectations for chip stocks are revised upward；Geopolitical competition → Export control risk rises → Supply chains become regionalized → Cost curve shifts upward
notes: AI guardrails are safeguards for AI, referring to regulatory limits on model capabilities, data use and deployment.
Why are chip stocks sensitive to regulation? If regulation forces AI companies to slow training and deployment, orders for GPUs and advanced chips will decline.
Capital expenditure is spending by cloud providers and technology companies on buying servers and chips and building data centers; it directly determines chip demand.
Advanced-node manufacturing and packaging are key stages in producing high-performance AI chips; chip prices and profit margins are more resilient when capacity is tight.
Export controls restrict the flow of high-end chips and equipment to China, forcing supply chains to split into different regions; building duplicate facilities raises costs.
Neither China nor the U.S. is willing to slow AI, meaning competition takes priority over safety coordination; risks of a policy backlash and supply chain friction remain over the long term.

tech.title: 7名博士生仅用3个月从零训练7B大模型：代码+数据+训练日志全公开
tech.raw_summary: 几百个Agent参与研发，AI开始造AI

insight.what: 7 名博士生用 3 个月从零训练出 70 亿参数大模型，公开代码、数据和训练日志，数百个 AI Agent 参与研发。
insight.why: 市场原本认为大模型训练被巨头算力和资本开支垄断；低成本复现降低训练门槛，改变算力需求结构，并挑战头部模型的稀缺性溢价。
insight.chain: 训练方法开源 → 大模型训练门槛下降 → 更多团队可自研模型 → 推理算力需求增加 → 云厂商和小型芯片需求上升 → 巨头模型稀缺性下降 → 头部 AI 估值溢价承压；AI Agent 参与研发 → 自动化研发效率提升 → 长期算力成本曲线下移
notes: 70 亿参数指模型内部可调权重数量，7B 属于中小型大模型，不是最前沿的万亿参数模型。
训练是从零学习海量数据，推理是模型训练完成后回答问题的过程，两者对芯片需求不同。
开源代码和训练日志让其他团队能复现，降低试错成本，削弱闭源模型的技术壁垒。
AI Agent 是能自主规划、调用工具和执行任务的 AI 程序，这里被用来辅助研发。
如果训练门槛下降，算力需求可能从少数巨头的大规模训练转向更多公司的推理和微调。
巨头模型稀缺性下降，意味着市场愿意给的估值溢价可能收窄，但拥有分发和数据的公司仍有优势。

insight_en.what: 7 doctoral students trained a 7-billion-parameter large model from scratch in 3 months and made the code, data and training logs public, with hundreds of AI agents participating in research and development.
insight_en.why: Markets had assumed that tech giants monopolized large-model training through their computing power and capital expenditure; low-cost replication lowers barriers to training, changes the composition of demand for computing capacity and challenges the scarcity premium of leading models.
insight_en.chain: Training methods are open-sourced → Barriers to large-model training fall → More teams can develop their own models → Demand for inference computing capacity increases → Cloud providers and small chips see rising demand → Tech giants' models become less scarce → Valuation premiums for AI leaders come under pressure；AI agents participate in research and development → Automated R&D becomes more efficient → Long-term computing cost curve shifts downward
notes: 7 billion parameters refers to the number of adjustable weights inside the model; 7B is a small- to medium-sized large model, not a cutting-edge trillion-parameter model.

Training is the process of learning from vast amounts of data from scratch, while inference is the process of answering questions after a model has been trained; the two have different chip requirements.
Open-source code and training logs enable replication by other teams, lowering trial-and-error costs and weakening the technological barriers of closed-source models.
An AI agent is an AI program that can autonomously plan, call tools and execute tasks; here, AI agents are used to assist research and development.
If barriers to training fall, demand for computing capacity may shift from large-scale training by a few tech giants to inference and fine-tuning by more companies.
As tech giants' models become less scarce, the valuation premium the market is willing to pay may narrow, but companies with distribution and data still have an advantage.
